chunks: The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “There is no salat for the neighbor of the mosque except in his mosque.” What is meant is that there is no especially virtuous salat of abundant reward, not that validity is negated in every respect.
As for what was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Bakr ibn Salih, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Imran, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

“When you perform wudu (ablution), then wipe your feet, their outer side and their inner side.” Then he said, “Like this,” so he placed his hand on the ankle and struck the other on the underside of his foot, then wiped them to the toes.

So this report is to be understood as taqiyyah, because it agrees with the doctrine of some of the general populace who hold the view of wiping and say that the entire foot must be covered, and that is contrary to the truth as we have explained.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, said: It is not permissible for anyone to make the place of wiping on his feet into washing, nor to replace the wiping of his head with washing it, just as it is not permissible to make the place of washing his face and hands into wiping. Rather, he must place wudu (ablution) in its proper places.
What the verse indicates is His saying, Exalted is He: “When you rise for salat, wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows, and wipe your heads and your feet up to the ankles.”

Thus, by the outward sense of the command, He made washing obligatory for the face and the hands, and made wiping obligatory for the head and the feet. Whoever wipes what Allah commanded to be washed, or washes what Allah commanded to be wiped, has not complied with the command, and opposing the command does not suffice. This is also indicated by further evidence.

key_terms.اَلتَّقِيَّةُ: dissimulation or precautionary conformity due to circumstances
key_terms.اَلْآيَةُ: the Quranic verse used as proof
key_terms.اَلْغَسْلَ: washing, the prescribed act for the face and hands
key_terms.اَلْكَعْبِ: the ankle, marking the area mentioned in wiping
key_terms.اَلْمَسْحَ: wiping, the prescribed act for the head and feet
key_terms.اَمْسَحْ: wipe; the commanded act in wudu for specific limbs
key_terms.قَدَمَيْكَ: your two feet, the limbs discussed in the ruling

ai.seo_question: Does wudu require wiping the feet or washing them according to Shi'i hadith and Quran?
ai.summary: This passage discusses rulings of wudu (ablution), especially the obligation of wiping the head and feet rather than washing them. It also interprets a report about wiping the whole foot as taqiyyah and supports the ruling through the Quranic verse on wudu, emphasizing that valid worship requires acting exactly according to the divine command.
